market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note with no broad directional market commentary from Adam. No explicit bull or bear market lean is provided.

company_items.summary: AZO beat FQ4 EPS at $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145bp tailwind to gross margins) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105bp tailwind) rather than operational strength. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100bp year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500MM upfront plus an additional ~$106.5MM. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90MM in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll reported solid FQ1 EPS of 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even without the tariff refund tailwind of 11 cents, implying 42 cents ex-refunds. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4MM vs. the Street's $943.2MM, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03B from $3.93-4.13B, while the EPS range was held unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no financial results attached.

THOR missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% vs. the Street's 13.85%, despite revenue coming in slightly above at $2.311B vs. the Street's $2.17B. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflationary pressures, and rising material costs as headwinds, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction initiatives, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking shares spiked in pre-market trading after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in the trial. The result is a meaningful clinical milestone in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug space. This positions Viking as a credible competitor in one of the most closely watched therapeutic categories in biopharma.

sectors: RV/recreational vehicle sector faces headwinds per THOR's commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, inflation, and margin pressure from rising material costs are weighing on the space. GLP-1/obesity drug sector gets a positive catalyst from Viking's VK2735 trial data showing 22% weight loss.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd — there's no broad macro or rates commentary in today's note, so let's go straight to the movers.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth fiscal quarter earnings at fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents — but the beat is low quality. The upside came from tariff refunds, a one hundred forty-five basis point tailwind to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO benefit worth another one hundred five basis points. Underneath that, domestic comps came in at plus one-point-six percent versus the Street's plus three-point-one percent, and the operating expense ratio worsened one hundred basis points year-over-year. Management did say sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter versus the first eight, and they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Mixed read overall.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront plus about one hundred six million more. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a bullish strategic move deeper into robotics and Physical AI.

MillerKnoll delivered a clean earnings beat — fifty-three cents versus the Street's thirty-six cents — and importantly, even stripping out the eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at forty-two cents. The miss on sales — down three-point-three percent organically to nine twenty-three versus the Street's nine forty-three — is the soft spot, though orders rose three-point-five percent year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed modestly while EPS guidance held steady. Mixed, leaning constructive on the earnings quality.

THOR Industries missed on fourth fiscal quarter earnings — seventy-eight cents versus the Street's eighty-seven cents. Gross margins fell two hundred thirty basis points year-over-year to twelve-point-four percent, well below the Street's thirteen-point-eight-five. Management's tone was cautious, pointing to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, inflation, and rising material costs. They expect a flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later in the fall. Some bright spots — healthy dealer inventory, structural cost actions underway, and a roughly seventy-five percent surge in North American towable RV order backlog — but the headline read is bearish.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the big pre-market mover. The company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing twenty-two percent weight loss. That's a headline number that gets attention in a space the market cares deeply about. Shares are spiking pre-market — this is a clear bullish catalyst.

Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November first. He's got prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition — watch for any market reaction but no financial catalyst here.

Bottom line for today: Viking is your high-beta momentum name on the GLP-1 result. AutoZone and MillerKnoll are mixed-quality beats worth monitoring for fade-or-follow setups. THOR is the clearest negative. Stay focused and size accordingly.
